pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: The Washington 01 General Journey Level Electrician exam is part of the electrical certification process administered through the Washington State Department of Labor & Industries. Electrician candidates must first apply to L&I and receive approval before registering for the PSI exam. After L&I approves an application, the candidate receives an eligibility notice with exam scheduling instructions and an Exam Unique ID used for PSI registration. The Washington electrical certification exam program is administered by PSI. The exam is computer-based, and candidates receive score reporting after completion. Washington’s PSI bulletin states that candidates must score 70% to pass. If a candidate does not pass, the score report includes diagnostic information by examination type so the candidate can identify weaker areas for additional study. For the 01 General Electrician classification, the electrician exam is divided into separate sections. The electrician sections listed for 01 General include NEC & Theory and WA Codes.

pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: The NEC & Theory section is listed with 60 questions and a 3-hour time allowance. The WA Codes section is listed with 17 questions and a 1-hour time allowance. Candidates should study both national code content and Washington electrical laws and rules because the exam requires knowledge of both. The NEC & Theory content outline for the 01 General Electrician exam includes NEC introduction, general requirements, wiring and protection, services, overcurrent protection, grounding and bonding, wiring methods, electrical equipment, motors, HVAC, generators, transformers, equipment over 600 volts, hazardous locations, special occupancies, special equipment, emergency and standby systems, special conditions, communication systems, and general trade knowledge and theory. The WA Codes section focuses on Washington laws and rules, including the state electrical law and administrative code content used for electrical work and electrical certification.

pieces.h: Open Book Test
pieces.t: Washington electrical certification exams are open book. The PSI bulletin states that candidates may use original copyrighted material and a silent, nonprinting, nonprogrammable calculator. Copies of Washington state RCW and WAC materials downloaded from the internet are acceptable when placed in a binder. Copyrighted materials may have highlighting, underlining, and permanent index tabs before entering the examination area. Open-book testing makes preparation with the correct materials especially important. The exam does not simply test whether a candidate owns a code book. It tests whether the candidate can identify the subject of a question, locate the correct article or rule, read the requirement carefully, and apply it under time pressure. Candidates who have not practiced code navigation may lose valuable exam time searching through the book. Washington’s rules do not allow Post-it notes, sticky notes, repositionable tabs, removable notes, or writing in references. Candidates should build study habits around clean, organized, exam-ready reference use.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: Washington journeyman electrician candidates begin by reviewing the current L&I electrical certification requirements for the 01 General Journey Level Electrician credential. Candidates must complete the required experience and training for their certificate type before submitting an application for examination. After L&I receives and verifies the application, the candidate is sent an eligibility notice with instructions for scheduling the exam through PSI. A practical path starts with building qualifying experience and training under Washington’s electrical licensing rules. For those pursuing the 01 journey level electrician certification, Washington has requirements tied to apprenticeship completion and documented experience. Candidates should keep accurate records and follow L&I instructions for documenting the work and training used to qualify for the exam. Once the candidate is ready to apply, the electrician application is submitted to L&I. After approval, the candidate uses the Exam Unique ID from the eligibility notice to register with PSI and schedule the exam.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Washington electrical licensing and certification are handled by the Washington State Department of Labor & Industries. To learn the electrical trade, individuals generally begin as electrical trainees and must work under the supervision of a certified electrician. Those learning to become 01 journey level electricians must follow Washington’s requirements for training, apprenticeship, and experience before qualifying for certification testing. Washington’s 01 General Journey Level Electrician credential is the broad journeyman-level electrical certification associated with general electrical work. Candidates pursuing this credential should focus on the requirements for the 01 General classification and the exam sections connected to that classification. Washington also has specialty electrical classifications, and the exam content differs by classification. Electrical candidates should understand that Washington’s exam expects knowledge of the National Electrical Code, Washington laws and rules, and electrical theory.

pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: The Washington electrical examination and certification process is administered through the Washington State Department of Labor & Industries. Candidates should confirm the exact credential they are pursuing before final exam preparation, because Washington distinguishes between electrician certification, electrical administrator certification, electrical contractor licensing, and master electrician status. Washington’s master electrician path is connected to advanced certification and administrator responsibility. A candidate may need to understand both the electrician certification side of the trade and the administrator side, depending on the credential and role being pursued. Electrical administrators are responsible for ensuring that electrical work performed by an electrical contractor complies with the applicable electrical laws and rules. Electrical contractors must also meet separate business licensing and registration requirements.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: The Washington licensing process begins with identifying the correct credential. Candidates should determine whether they are pursuing journey level electrician certification, specialty electrician certification, electrical administrator certification, master electrician recognition, electrical contractor licensing, or another electrical credential regulated by L&I. The correct path depends on the work the candidate plans to perform, supervise, qualify, administer, or contract for. After identifying the correct credential, candidates should review the Washington L&I application requirements. Electrician certification may require documented training hours, experience, education, trainee records, or prior certification. Administrator certification may require exam approval for the administrator category. Contractor licensing may require a business license, bond, insurance, administrator assignment, and other business requirements. Once the application path is clear, candidates prepare for the required exam using the applicable code edition and reference list.
